sourceAnchors.message: To be compliant to J2EE, a webapp should not use any thread.
sourceAnchors.reason: SS332 single-owner borrowed-connection read observes the current thread interrupt at entry and after both owned JDBC resources close. It creates no thread, executor, daemon or J2EE container work.

sourceAnchors.message: Ensure that resources like this PreparedStatement object are closed after use
sourceAnchors.reason: checked is a non-null alias of the acquired statement. Its original statement reference is closed exactly once in the outer finally after row close; explicit precedence is SS332. RRF-PURE-004/005/006 asserts acquired equals close count.

sourceAnchors.message: Ensure that resources like this ResultSet object are closed after use
sourceAnchors.reason: values is a non-null alias of the acquired ResultSet. The original row reference is closed exactly once in the inner finally, including projection/null/runtime/error failures; statement still closes afterward. RRF-PURE-004/005/006 checks counters.

sourceAnchors.sourceAnchor: final Map<String, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
sourceAnchors.message: If you run in Java5 or newer and have concurrent access, you should use the ConcurrentHashMap implementation
sourceAnchors.reason: Each Fixture is created inside one synchronous read or one independent virtual task and never escapes that owner. Its event/count/failure/bind maps are accessed only by that task. The concurrent test uses 32 separate fixtures, so no concurrent map access exists.

sourceAnchors.message: In J2EE, getClassLoader() might not work as expected.  Use Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader() instead.
sourceAnchors.reason: Only standard java.sql interfaces are proxied. The explicit loader owning the exact interface is required by Proxy.newProxyInstance; no contextual/plugin/product class loading or Class.forName is used.
